summary.text: Marlin Stutzman is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 3rd District. A fourth-generation farmer from Howe, he served in the Indiana House and Senate and in the U.S. House beginning in 2010, worked in manufacturing, agriculture and food-service businesses during a break from Congress, and returned to the U.S. House in 2025. He is seeking re-election to the seat.

paragraphs.text: Stutzman was born in Sturgis, Michigan, in 1976, graduated from Lake Area Christian High School and attended Trine State University.

According to his official biography, he is a fourth-generation farmer from Howe, Indiana, who started his own beef cattle operation at 16 and by 18 had joined his father and other family members in growing the family business.

Stutzman was elected to the Indiana House of Representatives at age 25 as its youngest serving member, and served from 2002 to 2008 while working full time in the family business. His official biography says he helped Gov. Mitch Daniels turn a $1 billion deficit into a surplus.
He then served one term in the Indiana State Senate, from 2009 to 2010.

Stutzman was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2010. His official biography says he authored the Conservative Congressional Budget and was the original sponsor of the Right to Try legislation, later signed into law by President Trump.

After leaving Congress he worked as an entrepreneur in manufacturing, agriculture and food service. According to his official biography, he and his wife, Christy, previously owned a farm-to-fork dinner theater with a meat processing facility that raised Wagyu beef.

He returned to the U.S. House in 2025 and serves on the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress. He is a member of the LaGrange Chamber of Commerce, National Federation of Independent Business, Indiana Farm Bureau, the Howe Community Association and the National Rifle Association.
